preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an AI system classifies a benign educational, contextual, analytical, explanatory, safety-oriented, or non-operational scientific request as restricted primarily because the subject belongs to a broad dual-use field. The system then refuses, pauses, reroutes, substitutes a less-capable model, or otherwise degrades the interaction without a sufficiently granular assessment of requested depth, operational applicability, optimisation potential, cumulative trajectory, evidence posture, and material harm uplift. The failure does not arise merely because a safety boundary exists. It arises when domain membership substitutes for depth-sensitive and trajectory-sensitive classification.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met where an interaction that should reasonably map to RDE-DS0/RDE-T1, RDE-DS1/RDE-T1-T2, or a permissible bounded RDE-DS2/RDE-T2 response is refused, paused, or routed away from the selected model principally because it concerns biology, biochemistry, medical science, chemistry, cybersecurity, or another dual-use domain, without evidence that the request seeks operationalisation, optimisation, harmful capability transfer, evasion, execution readiness, or another RDE-DS3/RDE-T3 condition. The threshold may also be met where model substitution occurs without sufficiently clear disclosure of the controlling classifier and resulting capability change.

preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: CAM already distinguishes general knowledge, contextual risk, constrained technical engagement, gated operational engagement, and absolute prohibition. A system that collapses an entire scientific field into a restricted class defeats that graduated architecture. Overbroad classification can suppress legitimate education and research, obscure the difference between safety policy and model capability, and deny users the higher-capability model they selected or paid to access. The correct control is not unrestricted disclosure. It is calibrated depth classification: preserve benign RDE-DS0/RDE-T1 and RDE-DS1/RDE-T1-T2 inquiry, permit bounded RDE-DS2/RDE-T2 technical explanation where it does not create material harm uplift, and reserve RDE-DS3/RDE-T3 gating for operational, optimisation-level, or execution-ready requests.
